findings.headline: Fed funds target range held at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent on 29 July 2026, unchanged since December 2025
findings.source_name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, FOMC statement 29 July 2026
findings.detail: Read from the Federal Reserve's own press release, not from a rate aggregator. The Committee 'decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent'.
findings.model_impact: ORAS reports in USD and 88.7% of its backlog is foreign currency or FCY-pegged, so the USD curve — not the EGP curve — anchors the explicit-window risk-free rate and the Kd on the group's floating-rate borrowings. Direction: a flat-to-higher USD path holds the discount rate up and the treasury income on USD 1.23bn of cash up with it.

findings.headline: Reporting currency is USD; the filing prints the exact translation rates used — EGP average 0.0203, closing 0.0210, opening 0.0197; SAR 0.2667; AED 0.2723; EUR 1.1729 closing
findings.source_name: FY2025 audited consolidated financial statements, note 6.3 'Significant rates'
findings.detail: The filing also states OC PLC 'is not exposed to Saudi Riyal, UAE Dirham and Qatar Riyal. These currencies are pegged to the US dollar.' Only the EGP and EUR legs float against the reporting currency.
findings.model_impact: DRIVER UNLOCK. The model is built in USD with an explicit EGP and EUR translation leg at the company's own published rates, rather than in EGP with a single blended devaluation assumption. Fixes the currency basis before any driver is set.

findings.headline: US Section 232 duties raised to 50% on primary steel, aluminium and copper articles and 25% on derivative articles effective 6 April 2026; in June 2026 the US-content threshold for the lower derivative rate was cut from 95% to 85%
findings.source_name: Construction Dive, 'What adjusted steel, aluminum and copper tariffs mean for construction'; Congressional Research Service IN12519 'Section 232 Tariffs on Steel and Aluminum'
findings.detail: External context for a cost driver, which is exactly what the outer rings are for. It is NOT used as a source for any ORAS reported number.
findings.model_impact: 'Changes in raw materials and consumables, finished goods and work in progress' was USD 3,970.7m in FY2025 — 78.6% of revenue and the single largest line in the cost stack. Tariffs set the USA-segment materials escalator UP and are the named mechanism behind the downside case on USA gross margin. One escalator for this line, separate from the labour escalator [Lessons Register L-009].

findings.headline: US data-centre construction running at roughly USD 50.7bn annualised in April 2026, +27.4% y/y; Big Four hyperscaler capex plans of about USD 630bn for 2026 against USD 388bn spent in 2025, with J.P. Morgan estimating USD 697bn across all hyperscalers
findings.source_name: J.P. Morgan, 'Financing AI infrastructure and U.S. data centers'; US Census construction-spending series as compiled by Axis Intelligence
findings.detail: Demand context for the USA segment. ORAS's own disclosure is the confirming leg: its US data-centre portfolio 'now exceeds 2 GW across multiple hyperscalers and developers' and the sector led H1-2026 awards.
findings.model_impact: Sets the USA new-awards growth rate in the explicit window. USA backlog rose 50.3% y/y to USD 3,963.7m at 30-Jun-2026 and USA new awards were 68.8% of group new awards in Q2-2026 alone; the hyperscaler capex path is the external check on whether that rate can persist.

findings.headline: Power interconnection queues, long-lead electrical gear and commissioning capacity — not capital — now set the pace of US data-centre delivery; an estimated 30-50% of planned 2026 AI data-centre capacity is expected to slip to 2028
findings.source_name: Build.inc, 'AI Infrastructure Capex Is Rewriting Data Center Development in 2026'; Axis Intelligence data-centre construction-spending analysis
findings.detail: The same analyses record the 'shell ratio' — US data-centre construction per dollar of Big Four capex — falling from 9.7 cents in 2025 to 7.0 cents in 2026, i.e. construction spend is growing far more slowly than the capital behind it.
findings.model_impact: Acts on TIMING, not on the award. Slows the burn rate of USA backlog into revenue rather than reducing new awards, so it is modelled as a lengthening of the backlog-to-revenue conversion period and not as a haircut to the order book.

findings.category: sovereign macro (inflation, policy rate, FX/deval risk)
findings.headline: CBE held rates on 20 August 2026: overnight deposit 19.00%, overnight lending 20.00%, main operation and discount 19.50%. Annual headline inflation 14.9% in July 2026 (core 14.7%), with monthly headline and core both 0.0%
findings.source_name: Egypt State Information Service report of the Central Bank of Egypt MPC decision of 20 August 2026
findings.detail: SOURCING EXCEPTION, STATED NOT HIDDEN: www.cbe.org.eg returned a 'Request Rejected' body at this environment's proxy on the sweep date (see the primary-access record), so this is the Egyptian government's own report of the CBE decision rather than the CBE's own print. It is used for external context only and touches no ORAS reported figure.
findings.model_impact: Sets the EGP-leg cost of debt and the Egypt labour and local-materials escalator. It is deliberately a SECOND-ORDER input, not the discount rate: only 11.3% of backlog is EGP-denominated, so an EGP policy rate cannot be allowed to drive a USD-reporting contractor's WACC.

findings.category: sovereign macro (inflation, policy rate, FX/deval risk)
findings.headline: EGP translation path from the filings themselves: 0.0197 USD/EGP at 1-Jan-2025, 0.0203 average 2025, 0.0210 at 31-Dec-2025. The company's own website quoted EGP 855.85 and AED 60.30 for the same share on the sweep date, implying roughly 52 EGP per USD in September 2026
findings.source_name: FY2025 audited financial statements note 6.3; orascom.com live share header, 08-Sep-2026
findings.detail: The EGP APPRECIATED against the USD through 2025 on the company's own published rates (0.0197 -> 0.0210) and has given that back since. Both directions are in the record so the build cannot quietly assume a one-way devaluation.
findings.model_impact: DRIVER UNLOCK for the FX leg. Because 75.2% of the Egypt backlog is itself in foreign currency, EGP moves are largely a TRANSLATION effect on a minority of revenue rather than an economic hit to margin. The model carries an explicit EGP translation line and does not apply a devaluation haircut to the whole Egypt segment.

findings.headline: OC PLC was continued into the Abu Dhabi Global Market effective 30 October 2025 (registered number 31025), from the DIFC where it was number 1752; audited under IFRS and the ADGM Companies Regulations 2020 and Markets Law No. 1 of 2012 by KPMG Lower Gulf Limited. UAE Pillar Two Domestic Minimum Top-up Tax has applied since 1 January 2025 and the group meets the transitional safe harbour (effective tax rate above 16%). Statutory rates across jurisdictions range 0.0% to 32.0%; the effective rate was 9.5% in FY2025 against 20.3% in FY2024
findings.source_name: FY2025 audited consolidated financial statements, note 1 and notes 11.1/11.2
findings.detail: The FY2025 reconciliation prints tax at the weighted average group rate of 18.3% (USD 41.5m), less USD 14.7m for recognition of a previously unrecognised tax asset, less USD 5.2m 'other', giving USD 21.6m. Unrecognised losses of USD 587.3m carry a USD 152.7m tax effect, of which USD 512.0m expires 2034-2037 and USD 75.3m never expires.
findings.model_impact: Tax is built from this reconciliation — weighted average group rate plus a separately modelled deferred-tax-asset recognition line — never as one blended statutory rate. The 9.5% FY2025 effective rate is NOT carried forward as a run rate: it contains a one-off DTA recognition that the reconciliation names.

findings.headline: Single-customer concentration: the Egyptian Government was 31.9% of FY2025 revenue, up from 27.3% in FY2024 — the only customer above the 10% disclosure threshold
findings.source_name: FY2025 audited consolidated financial statements, note 26 segment reporting
findings.model_impact: Ties the Egypt revenue leg directly to the Egyptian state budget, so the public-investment ceiling below is a hard cap on that leg rather than background colour. Also the receivable-risk driver: collection timing on state work sets DSO.

findings.category: fiscal / political events with sector read-through
findings.headline: Egypt's public investment ceiling was EGP 1,158bn in FY2025/26 (5.4% of GDP) and is raised to EGP 1.2tn for FY2026/27, alongside EGP 1.9tn of targeted private investment; the IMF completed the seventh EFF review in July 2026, disbursing USD 1.8bn, with the primary surplus going from 4.8% to 5.0% of GDP
findings.source_name: IMF Country Report No. 26/69 and IMF press release PR26/231 (Egypt, seventh EFF review); Egyptian Ministry of Planning FY2026/27 Economic and Social Development Plan as reported by The Middle East Observer
findings.detail: The IMF programme's own condition is 'strengthening the evaluation and prioritization of all public investment projects', i.e. the ceiling is binding and enforced rather than indicative.
findings.model_impact: Caps Egypt new-award growth in the explicit window. Egypt is 45.3% of the 30-Jun-2026 backlog and the Egyptian Government is 31.9% of revenue, so a ceiling growing at roughly 4% in nominal EGP against ~15% inflation is a REAL contraction in the domestic order pool — the mechanism behind the MEA-share decline already visible in the backlog mix (Egypt 54.3% at FY2025 -> 50.5% at Q1-2026 -> 45.3% at H1-2026).

findings.headline: Saudi construction forecast to grow ~5.4% a year to 2029 on a USD 1.65tn project pipeline, the third largest globally; UAE pipeline near USD 875bn; Saudi awards of SAR 29.5bn (USD 7.9bn) across 25 contracts in June 2026 alone
findings.source_name: MEED, 'Why 2026 is a breakthrough year for Middle East construction' and MEED GCC 2026 Projects Outlook; King & Spalding, 'Outlook and Opportunities in GCC Projects into 2026 and Beyond'
findings.detail: MEED's own framing is that 2025 awards FELL and 2026 stays busy on previously awarded work flowing through — a distinction that matters for a backlog-burn model.
findings.model_impact: Sets the regional (non-Egypt MEA) new-awards growth rate. KSA is 8.7% and the UAE 6.6% of backlog at 30-Jun-2026, both rising, and this is the pool they are rising into.

findings.headline: The observable price/cost outcome by region, from the company's own reporting: EBITDA margin MEA 8.3% FY2025 and 8.7% H1-2026; USA 3.1% FY2025 and 4.7% H1-2026, with USA H1-2026 EBITDA up 219.3% y/y on 84.3% revenue growth
findings.source_name: Q2-2026 results announcement, 14 August 2026, and FY-2025 results announcement, 31 March 2026, Summary Financial Results tables
findings.detail: Both tables foot: H1-2026 EBITDA MEA 131.3 + USA 69.6 = 200.9, revenue MEA 1,502.3 + USA 1,475.7 = 2,978.0. There is no contract-price index and no disclosed price per unit of work — see the negative search F55.
findings.model_impact: These are RECONCILIATION TARGETS, not inputs. Gross and EBITDA margin are computed from the cost stack and then checked against these printed regional margins; a build that has to type one of them in has failed. The USA margin RISE against a falling MEA share is the single most important mix effect in the model.

findings.headline: Named regional competitors are scaling: Hassan Allam Holding reported 2025 revenue of about USD 2.1bn with a backlog above USD 7.2bn across 100+ projects in Egypt, Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Oman; The Arab Contractors and Elsewedy Electric jointly delivered Tanzania's USD 2.9bn Julius Nyerere hydropower project; Hassan Allam, Arab Contractors, Concord and Orascom Construction were the four Contractor-of-the-Year finalists at the 2026 Big 5 Egypt Awards
findings.source_name: Forbes Middle East Top 100 Arab Family Businesses 2026 (Hassan Allam Holding); Zawya and Billionaires.Africa reporting of named Hassan Allam awards; Amwal Al Ghad, Big 5 Egypt Awards 2026 shortlist
findings.detail: Competitor data is used for the relative-multiple lens and for award-share pressure ONLY. It is never a source for any ORAS figure [SIGCM clause 5].
findings.model_impact: Caps ORAS's share of the Egyptian and regional award pool, which is the constraint on the MEA new-awards driver. A backlog of USD 7.2bn at one private domestic rival against ORAS's USD 6.9bn MEA backlog is the reason MEA award growth is modelled flat-to-modest while USA growth carries the forecast.

findings.headline: No substitution threat to on-site heavy civil EPC inside the forecast horizon. The modular and prefabricated construction market reached about USD 183.4bn in 2026, but EPC modularisation is concentrated in remote mining and offshore oil and gas, and the observed pattern is hybrid delivery — large prefabricated modules plus traditional site finishing — rather than replacement
findings.source_name: AVEVA, 'Modular construction: a storied alternative for EPC firms'; Future Market Insights, Modular & Prefabricated Construction Market; Modular Building Institute
findings.detail: Recorded as a searched-and-closed category rather than assumed. The live technology question for this issuer is the opposite of substitution: data-centre and HVDC work is technology DEMAND, and ORAS's ENR Telecommunications rank of #4 is the evidence.

findings.headline: ENR's 2026 rankings, published August 2026: Orascom Construction #29 on the Top 250 International Contractors, up 11 places from #40 in 2025; #91 on the Top 250 Global Contractors, up 36 from #127; #8 in Africa (from #10); #8 in the USA, a NEW entry; #4 in Telecommunications (from #5), on data-centre work. ENR's Top 250 international revenue as a group rose 9.7% to USD 550.6bn
findings.source_name: Engineering News-Record 2026 Top 250 International Contractors and Top 250 Global Contractors, reported in Orascom Construction's announcement of 29 August 2026
findings.detail: Third-party ranking, relayed in the company's own announcement. A rank is a relative measure of revenue earned outside the home country, so moving from #40 to #29 while the whole cohort grew 9.7% is independent corroboration that the USA expansion is real share gain, not a currency or definition artefact. The #8-in-the-USA new entry is the single most load-bearing item here.
findings.model_impact: Independent corroboration for the USA revenue driver. It supports carrying the USA growth rate ABOVE the US market rate in the early explicit years rather than converging it immediately, and it supplies the peer set for the relative-multiple lens.

findings.headline: FY2025 audited: revenue USD 5,049.8m, cost of sales (4,588.3), gross profit 461.5, other income 16.3, SG&A (205.6), operating profit 272.2, net finance cost (84.1), equity-accounted income 39.2, PBT 227.3, tax (21.6), net profit 205.7, attributable to owners 194.8, NCI 10.9, EPS USD 1.77
findings.source_name: Orascom Construction PLC FY2025 audited consolidated financial statements (KPMG Lower Gulf Limited, signed 30 March 2026)
findings.model_impact: The base year. Every forecast line is anchored on these printed figures, and the FY2025 gross margin is a CHECK on the rebuilt cost stack, never an input to it.

findings.headline: FY2024 audited: revenue USD 3,254.9m, cost of sales (2,952.0), gross profit 302.9, operating profit 120.1, PBT 167.9, net profit 133.8, attributable 118.0, EPS USD 1.07
findings.source_name: Orascom Construction PLC FY2024 audited consolidated financial statements
findings.detail: Footed: 3,254.9 - 2,952.0 = 302.9; 302.9 + 15.0 - 197.8 = 120.1; 120.1 + 17.8 + 30.0 = 167.9; 167.9 - 34.1 = 133.8; 118.0 + 15.8 = 133.8. Gross margin 9.31%. FY2024 finance income of 128.7 contains a USD 106.8m foreign-exchange GAIN — FY2024 is not a clean comparative below operating profit and the model treats it accordingly.
findings.model_impact: Second historical year and the reason the reconciliation table must split operating from FX effects: the FY2024-to-FY2025 net profit bridge is dominated by a non-recurring FX swing, not by operations.

findings.headline: FY2023 audited: revenue USD 3,367.5m, cost of sales (3,099.7), gross profit 267.8, other income 130.0, SG&A (195.6), operating profit 202.2, PBT 228.4, net profit 195.1, attributable 158.6
findings.source_name: Orascom Construction PLC FY2023 audited consolidated financial statements
findings.detail: Footed: 3,367.5 - 3,099.7 = 267.8; 267.8 + 130.0 - 195.6 = 202.2; 202.2 + 5.5 + 20.7 = 228.4; 228.4 - 33.3 = 195.1. Gross margin 7.95% — the LOW of the four years. Note the outsized USD 130.0m 'other income' line, which is why FY2023 operating profit looks strong on a weak gross margin.
findings.model_impact: Third historical year and the low-water mark for gross margin; it sets the floor of the margin range the rebuilt cost stack has to be able to reproduce.

findings.headline: FY2022 audited: revenue USD 4,177.3m, cost of sales (3,830.4), gross profit 346.9, operating profit 154.7, PBT 171.9, net profit 134.3, attributable 113.5. The same filing prints FY2021: revenue 3,542.9, gross profit 346.4, attributable 113.4
findings.source_name: Orascom Construction PLC FY2022 audited consolidated financial statements
findings.detail: Footed: 4,177.3 - 3,830.4 = 346.9; 346.9 + 5.1 - 197.3 = 154.7; 154.7 - 18.0 + 35.2 = 171.9; 171.9 - 37.6 = 134.3. Gross margin 8.30%. The FOUR-YEAR TARGET IS MET: FY2022, FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 all read from the filings themselves, with FY2021 available as a fifth year of comparatives.
findings.model_impact: Fourth historical year. Together the four give a gross-margin range of 7.95%-9.31% on revenue swinging from 3.25bn to 5.05bn — which is the evidence that margin is NOT a stable input and has to be produced by the cost build.

findings.headline: FY2025 balance sheet (read by OCR off the rendered page — the text layer is empty): total assets USD 5,215.8m, total equity 900.7, total liabilities 4,315.1. Non-current assets 859.6 including equity-accounted investees 540.0; current assets 4,356.2 including cash 1,369.7, trade and other receivables 1,902.5 and contracts work in progress 807.8. FY2024 comparative: assets 3,971.3, equity 647.5, liabilities 3,323.8
findings.source_name: Orascom Construction PLC FY2025 audited consolidated financial statements, printed page 9 / PDF page 11
findings.detail: ROUTE RECORDED. PDF page 11 carries 0 characters of text and one embedded image; pdftoppm -r 300 -gray then tesseract --psm 6 --oem 1. Every block foots: 178.5 + 27.7 + 33.1 + 540.0 + 80.3 = 859.6; 275.4 + 1,902.5 + 807.8 + 0.8 + 1,369.7 = 4,356.2; 859.6 + 4,356.2 = 5,215.8; 110.2 + 467.3 - 448.9 + 743.9 = 872.5, + 28.2 NCI = 900.7; 111.8 + 4,203.3 = 4,315.1; 900.7 + 4,315.1 = 5,215.8. The one OCR failure — non-current loans and borrowings read as '—' and '75' — does NOT foot and was resolved to 31.2 (FY2025) and 7.5 (FY2024) by subtraction and confirmed against note 18's text layer. Arithmetic was the arbiter.
findings.model_impact: Opening balance sheet for the projection. Equity-accounted investees of 540.0 and cash of 1,369.7 together are 36.6% of total assets, so the equity bridge is dominated by items OUTSIDE the operating business and cannot be modelled as a residual.

findings.headline: THE COST STACK. Note 21 expenses by nature, FY2025 (FY2024): changes in raw materials, consumables, finished goods and WIP 3,970.7 (2,446.0); employee benefit expenses 679.5 (587.0); depreciation and amortisation 32.8 (31.4); maintenance and repairs 38.9 (24.7); consultancy 27.5 (15.7); donations 0.9 (3.6); other 43.6 (41.4); total 4,793.9 (3,149.8). The same note exists in FY2022, FY2023 and FY2024
findings.source_name: FY2025 audited consolidated financial statements note 21; FY2024 note 22; FY2023 note 22; FY2022 note 21
findings.detail: THE IDENTITY THAT MAKES MARGIN AN OUTPUT: the note total equals cost of sales plus SG&A EXACTLY in every year — FY2025 4,588.3 + 205.6 = 4,793.9; FY2024 2,952.0 + 197.8 = 3,149.8; FY2023 3,099.7 + 195.6 = 3,295.3; FY2022 3,830.4 + 197.3 = 4,027.7. Each column also foots internally. A 0.1 reclassification between D&A and 'other' appears in the FY2022 comparative shown inside the FY2023 filing (45.6/55.5 against the FY2022 filing's own 45.5/55.6); the total is unchanged.
findings.model_impact: DRIVER UNLOCK, and the single most important finding in this register. Cost is built line by line by nature with its OWN escalator each, and gross margin is then whatever falls out. Materials at 78.6% of FY2025 revenue and labour at 13.5% are the two that matter; setting a contribution or gross margin as an input here would be a QC FAIL because the filings disclose enough to build the cost instead [Lessons Register L-005].

findings.headline: Headcount and labour cost paired: 60,231 employees at 31-Dec-2025 (24,452 permanent, 35,779 temporary; 15,343 engineering, 44,888 non-engineering) against 56,119 at 31-Dec-2024. Employee benefit expense USD 679.5m splits into wages and salaries 534.6, employee profit sharing 44.7, pension 7.0, social security 1.1 and other 92.1
findings.source_name: FY2025 audited consolidated financial statements, note 21(ii)
findings.detail: Both splits foot: 24,452 + 35,779 = 60,231 and 15,343 + 44,888 = 60,231; 534.6 + 1.1 + 44.7 + 7.0 + 92.1 = 679.5. Average cost per head is therefore USD 11,282 in FY2025 against USD 10,460 in FY2024, +7.9%. The LTIP is cash-settled with 5,320,798 shares outstanding under it and a carrying value of USD 67.6m (FY2024: 30.1m); USD 16.7m vested in FY2025.
findings.model_impact: DRIVER UNLOCK: labour becomes cost-per-head x heads, with heads driven off the backlog and cost-per-head off its own escalator, rather than a percentage of revenue. The LTIP's carrying value more than doubling is a separately modelled accrual, not part of the per-head rate.

findings.headline: Percentage-of-completion basis, stated and quantified: revenue on construction contracts is a single performance obligation recognised OVER TIME using a cost-based input method; costs incurred on contracts including estimated earnings were USD 26,223.7m against billings to date of 26,401.9, a net (178.2). Of FY2025 revenue, 4,985.3 was transferred over time and only 64.5 at a point in time
findings.source_name: FY2025 audited consolidated financial statements, notes 3 (revenue policy), 13 and 25, and the KPMG key audit matter on revenue recognition
findings.detail: The auditor's key audit matter names the mechanism precisely: 'Progress is assessed with reference to the proportion of contract costs incurred for the work performed as at the reporting date, relative to the estimated total costs of the contract at completion.' Foots: 26,223.7 - 26,401.9 = (178.2), and (178.2) = contract assets 807.8 less billings in excess 986.0. FY2024: 21,439.3 - 21,419.2 = 20.1 = 575.7 - 555.6.
findings.model_impact: DRIVER UNLOCK, and it fixes the model's clock. Because progress is cost-to-cost, revenue and cost are recognised on the SAME clock — so the failure Lessons Register L-001 records (revenue as you build, cost on handover) cannot occur here, and revenue is projected as cost incurred divided by the estimated cost ratio rather than as a growth rate.

findings.headline: NET CASH ON THE COMPANY'S OWN DEFINITION (capital-management note: loans and borrowings less cash and cash equivalents), six dates from six filings: FY2021 (441.6); FY2022 (325.7); FY2023 (446.8); FY2024 (728.1); FY2025 (1,054.8); 31-Mar-2026 (875.4); 30-Jun-2026 (731.0). Total equity on the same dates: 688.6 / 691.3 / 711.4 / 647.5 / 900.7 / 927.6 / 1,022.6
findings.source_name: Capital-management note in each filing: FY2022 note 6.4, FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 note 6.4, Q1-2026 and H1-2026 reviewed statements
findings.detail: Every pair foots: 314.9 - 1,369.7 = (1,054.8) at FY2025; 499.1 - 1,230.1 = (731.0) at 30-Jun-2026; 313.2 - 1,041.3 = (728.1) at FY2024. THE COMPANY'S DEFINITION EXCLUDES TWO THINGS THE BUILD MUST DECIDE ON: lease obligations (USD 31.4m at FY2025, inside trade and other payables) and, from H1-2026, USD 139.4m of excess cash reclassified to 'investment in financial assets at FVTPL' — so the disclosed (731.0) understates economic net cash by that 139.4.
findings.model_impact: Sets the capital structure and the EV-to-equity bridge. The group is net cash on every date in the record, so the WACC is close to all-equity and the bridge ADDS net cash. The FVTPL reclassification is added back explicitly and the choice is disclosed rather than silently following the company's definition.

findings.headline: Debt composition by borrower and tenor, note 18. At 31-Dec-2025 total USD 314.9m: Orascom Construction SAE 230.9 (bank facilities, current), Fayoum for Warehouse and Depots 30.9 (long term, maturing July 2039), Orascom Road Construction 25.6, The Weitz Group LLC 11.5, National Steel Fabrication 12.5, other 3.5. Split 31.2 long-term / 11.2 short-term / 272.5 bank facilities. ALL of it is floating rate; a 10% move in rates moves profit before tax by USD 9.2m
findings.source_name: FY2025 audited consolidated financial statements, notes 18 and 6.3
findings.detail: Foots: 230.9 + 30.9 + 25.6 + 11.5 + 12.5 + 3.5 = 314.9, and 31.2 + 11.2 + 272.5 = 314.9. FY2024: 235.9 + 32.7 + 22.6 + 12.5 + 6.9 + 2.6 = 313.2. Borrowings ROSE to 499.1 by 30-Jun-2026 on the Q2 working-capital outflow, which the release attributes to 'working capital timing in Egypt related to higher billings and projects under approval'.
findings.model_impact: Kd is built from named facilities at their own rates, never from interest expense over total current liabilities [Lessons Register L-002]. The 100%-floating disclosure means Kd tracks the policy path directly and is not fixed by a coupon. The borrower list also gives the currency of each tranche by domicile — a mostly-EGP borrower base against a mostly-USD revenue base.

findings.headline: Currency exposure table, note 6.3. At 31-Dec-2025: EUR cash and borrowings 274.1, EUR receivables 2.0, EUR payables (2.0); EGP cash and borrowings (219.5), EGP receivables 673.6, EGP payables (1,215.6), plus EGP forward contracts with a notional of 170.6. A 10% move gives +/-27.4 on PBT for EUR and +/-18.4 on PBT and (59.1) on equity for EGP; USD-denominated items held by non-USD entities add about 50.0
findings.source_name: FY2025 audited consolidated financial statements, note 6.3 market risk
findings.detail: The company states the exposure is 'not actively managed, nor is it hedged' for translation, and that functional currencies across the group are 'primarily Euro, US Dollar, Egyptian Pound, Saudi Riyal, Algerian Dinar and UAE Dirham'. EGP payables at (1,215.6) nearly doubled from (629.0) a year earlier — a net EGP SHORT of roughly 761.5 at FY2025.
findings.model_impact: Splits the FX driver in two: a translation leg on EGP and EUR net assets, and a transaction leg on the net EGP monetary short. The net short means EGP WEAKNESS is a profit-and-loss GAIN on monetary items even as it is an equity loss on translation — the two must not be netted into one devaluation assumption.

findings.headline: Equity-accounted investees, note 10. BESIX Group SA 50.0% held through OC IHC 3 B.V., carried at USD 459.9m (FY2024: 417.3). BESIX at 100%: net assets 919.8, construction revenue 4,849.6, construction cost (4,800.2), net profit 49.4 — so the group's 50% share is 24.7. Seven other associates: Red Sea Wind Energy 25% (42.7), National Pipe 40% (15.2), Ras Ghareb Wind 20% (7.1), Orasqualia 50% (6.2), Wave Co Development SPV 33.3% (5.1), Al Ahly for Industrial Development 25% (3.7). Total carrying value 540.0
findings.source_name: FY2025 audited consolidated financial statements, note 10
findings.detail: Foots: opening 450.0 + additions 35.1 + share of results 39.2 - dividends 16.1 + FX 31.8 = 540.0. BESIX's own construction margin is 1.02% (49.4 on 4,849.6) — an order of magnitude below the parent's, which is why BESIX is modelled as a separate equity-method leg and never blended into group margin. SPA signed with OCI Global N.V. on 9 December 2025; ORAS shareholders approved all special resolutions at the general meeting of 22 January 2026. ORAS will issue 97,201,359 NEW shares at USD 1 nominal plus a USD 12.79 premium, taking issued capital from 110,243,935 to 207,445,294 shares (+88.2%). The target is a Dutch company receiving substantially all of OCI's assets and liabilities: OCI Nitrogen in the Netherlands, an associated terminal asset under a signed SPA for EUR 290m expected to close in H1 2026, a 12.9% stake in Methanex and a large cash position. findings.source_name: Orascom Construction PLC Shareholders' Circular (OC-PLC-Shareholders-Circular-EN.pdf, 8 January 2026) and the Q2-2026 results announcement of 14 August 2026

Two published cases: standalone ORAS on 110.2m shares, and post-combination ORAS on 207.4m shares carrying a nitrogen and methanol business plus the target's cash. Per-share value is not comparable across the two, and the headline range must say which it is. The circular's own USD 13.79 per share is a disclosed reference point, NOT a fair value.

findings.headline: DUAL LISTING — TWO LEGITIMATE REGRESSORS, AND THE SERIES DECIDES. Audited FS note 1: the ordinary shares are 'dual listed on the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange (ADX) and the Egyptian Exchange (EGX) (previously dual listed on NASDAQ Dubai and the Egyptian Exchange)'. The company's IR share-information block separates them: ADX is the PRIMARY listing, ISIN AEE01702O253, currency AED, ticker ORAS; EGX is the SECONDARY listing, ISIN EGS95001C011, currency EGP, ticker ORAS; 110,243,935 shares; incorporation ADGM, Abu Dhabi. On the sweep date orascom.com's own page header quoted BOTH at once: EGP 855.85 and AED 60.30, a ratio of 14.19x
findings.source_name: FY2025 audited consolidated financial statements note 1; orascom.com Investors Updates share-information block and live site header, 08-Sep-2026
findings.detail: RESOLUTION OF THE TRAP FOR THIS REPO. engine/raw_ohlc/EG/ORAS.csv holds 2,773 daily rows from 11-Mar-2015 to 23-Aug-2026 and closes at 782.25 — the same order of magnitude as the company's own EGP quote of 855.85 two weeks later and roughly 15x the AED quote, so the stored series is the EGX/EGP series and is filed under the correct market code EG. A conforming beta on that series regresses against engine/raw_indices/EG/EGX30.csv, which the repo holds; the ADX alternative would require an ADX index (engine/raw_indices/AE holds FADGI, ADXGENERAL and DFMGI). A magnitude cross-check on the ADX side, labelled as an aggregator and used for MARKET DATA ONLY, puts ORAS near AED 51.95 in July 2026 on a 52-week range of AED 28.60-59.00 (stockanalysis.com), consistent with the AED 60.30 the company itself quotes. TWO COMPLICATIONS THE BUILD MUST HANDLE, NOT ASSUME AWAY: the ADX line replaced a Nasdaq Dubai line inside the historical window (the January-2025 shareholding disclosure still names AEDFXA14NUL7 / Nasdaq Dubai, and a liquidity provider was appointed on ADX on 11 September 2025), and the EGX series is denominated in a currency that moved from roughly 47.6 to 52 per USD over the same period. NO BETA IS RESOLVED HERE. Per the standing rule the number itself comes only from engine/beta_regression.own_stock_beta(); a study-local regression is never hand-rolled.
findings.model_impact: Fixes the REGRESSOR SELECTION, which is the input to the cost of equity. Choose EG/EGX30 to match the EGP series already held, or source an ADX/AED series and regress against an ADX index — but never mix a price in one currency with an index from the other exchange. The FERTIGLB precedent is the warning: the wrong regressor moved beta 0.492 against 0.931 and fair value by 21.6%.

drivers.driver: Construction revenue — MEA segment (opening backlog x burn rate + new awards)
drivers.justification: Built from the disclosed MEA backlog of USD 6,915.3m at 30-Jun-2026, the disclosed MEA new awards of 2,067.2 in H1-2026, and the four years of audited MEA revenue (2,812.9 / 1,809.7 / 1,611.3 / 2,849.3) that calibrate the burn rate. The Egypt and other-MEA legs are split using the presentation's finer revenue geography (Egypt 36.2%, other MEA 14.2% of H1-2026 revenue), which the audited MENA/USA split does not give. The Egypt leg is capped by the public investment ceiling and the 31.9% government-customer concentration.

drivers.driver: Construction revenue — USA segment (opening backlog x burn rate + new awards)
drivers.justification: Built from the disclosed USA backlog of USD 3,963.7m at 30-Jun-2026 (+50.3% y/y), USA new awards of 2,762.6 in H1-2026, and four years of audited USA revenue (1,364.4 / 1,557.8 / 1,643.6 / 2,200.5). The award growth rate is sanity-checked against hyperscaler capex and the ENR rank move from #40 to #29 internationally with a new #8 in the USA; the CONVERSION rate is slowed for the grid and long-lead-equipment constraint rather than the award being cut.

drivers.driver: Cost stack — raw materials, consumables and work in progress (per unit of work)
drivers.justification: Note 21 discloses this line for four years (FY2025 USD 3,970.7m, 78.6% of revenue) and it ties exactly to cost of sales plus SG&A. Because progress is measured cost-to-cost, this line IS the percentage-of-completion input, so it is projected as cost incurred against the estimated total contract cost and escalated on its own index — with the Section 232 tariff schedule setting the USA leg's escalator separately from the MEA leg's.

drivers.driver: Cost stack — employee benefit expense (cost per head x headcount)
drivers.justification: The filing pairs USD 679.5m of employee benefit expense with 60,231 employees (56,119 a year earlier), split permanent/temporary and engineering/non-engineering, and splits the cost into wages, profit sharing, pension, social security and other. Cost per head is USD 11,282 in FY2025 against 10,460 in FY2024. Headcount is driven off the backlog; the rate is escalated on Egyptian and US wage inflation SEPARATELY, never on one blended index.

drivers.driver: Cost stack — D&A, maintenance and repairs, consultancy and other
drivers.justification: All four lines are disclosed by nature for four years and foot to the total (FY2025: 32.8 + 38.9 + 27.5 + 0.9 + 43.6). D&A is projected off the PP&E roll-forward and the disclosed investment in PP&E; the rest are projected on their own historic relationship to activity rather than folded into an overhead rate.

drivers.driver: Gross margin — COMPUTED OUTPUT, never an input
drivers.justification: Gross margin is revenue less the built cost stack, full stop. The four audited years give 8.30% / 7.95% / 9.31% / 9.14% and the study year has printed 10.02% in Q1-2026 and 9.43% in Q2-2026 — a range wide enough that typing a margin in would decide the answer. The printed regional EBITDA margins (MEA 8.7%, USA 4.7% in H1-2026) are RECONCILIATION TARGETS the build has to reproduce, not inputs to it [Lessons Register L-005].

drivers.driver: Selling, general and administrative expenses
drivers.justification: SG&A is not a separate cost pool in this issuer: note 21's expenses by nature covers cost of sales AND SG&A together and ties exactly. SG&A is therefore built as the residual of the same by-nature build (FY2025 205.6 on a 4,793.9 total) with its own labour and consultancy components, rather than as a percentage of revenue.

drivers.driver: Segment gross margin split (MEA versus USA)
drivers.justification: TOP-DOWN BY NECESSITY AND THE GAP IS FLAGGED. The segment note stops at revenue, D&A, interest and profit before tax — it discloses NO cost of sales and NO gross profit by segment, and expenses by nature is group-wide only. The segment split is therefore allocated from the group cost stack using the disclosed regional EBITDA and PBT as the constraint, and the allocation is shown as an assumption rather than a disclosure. Dropping a level and saying so is the rule; going quiet about it is not.

drivers.driver: BESIX equity-method income (50%)
drivers.justification: Built from BESIX's OWN disclosed figures at 100% — construction revenue 4,849.6, construction cost (4,800.2), net profit 49.4, net assets 919.8 — taken at the disclosed 50.0%, with the standalone backlog of EUR 6,293.9m at 30-Jun-2026 driving the revenue path. BESIX's 1.02% construction margin is an order of magnitude below the parent's, so it is never blended into group margin, and its EUR 209.1m net cash sits outside the parent's net-cash line.

drivers.driver: Concessions — per asset (MW and m3/day x ownership)
drivers.justification: Every operational concession is disclosed with its capacity, ownership percentage, contract duration and its own H1-2026 revenue: Red Sea Wind 650 MW at 25% (USD 30.4m), Ras Ghareb 263 MW at 20% (20.7m), Orasqualia 250 m3/day at 50% (5.5m), plus Dammam ISTP and the Fayoum warehouse. Ras Shukheir 900 MW at 25% is modelled from its own PPA date and expected Q3-2026 financial close, not assumed into the base. Distributions received were USD 6.1m in H1-2026.

drivers.driver: Building materials, equipment services and facility management subsidiaries
drivers.justification: Each unit is disclosed with ownership, capacity and its own H1-2026 revenue at 100%: National Steel Fabrication (50k tons/year, USD 31.8m), Orascom Services (25.1m), Contrack FM (13.9m), Integrated Facade Solutions (11.4m), National Pipe (86 km/yr, 5.9m at 40%), Orascom Industrial Parks (15.5m sqm, 2.7m at 60.5%). Built per unit against capacity, with the segment's disclosed USD 8.0m H1-2026 net profit contribution as the check.

drivers.driver: Net finance cost and treasury income
drivers.justification: Kd is built from the named facilities in note 18 — six borrowers, USD 314.9m at FY2025 rising to 499.1m at 30-Jun-2026, 100% floating — at each borrower's own market rate, and NOT from interest expense over total current liabilities [Lessons Register L-002]. Treasury income is modelled on the disclosed cash of 1,230.1m plus the 139.4m reclassified to FVTPL. The disclosed sensitivity of USD 9.2m of PBT per 10% rate move is the calibration check.

drivers.driver: Effective tax rate
drivers.justification: Built from the disclosed reconciliation: the weighted average group rate (18.3% in FY2025, 28.9% in FY2024) applied to pre-tax profit, with the deferred-tax-asset recognition line modelled separately against the USD 587.3m of unrecognised losses and their 2034-2037 expiry. The 9.5% FY2025 effective rate is NOT carried forward as a run rate because the reconciliation names the one-off inside it. UAE Pillar Two safe-harbour status is tracked as a risk.

drivers.driver: Working capital — receivables, retentions, advances and billings in excess
drivers.justification: Every component is disclosed. At 30-Jun-2026 receivables split into USD 1,079.4m accounts receivable, 333.0 retentions and 569.8 supplier and subcontractor advances, with 71% of gross trade receivables not yet due; payables into 583.8 trade, 1,043.8 accrued and 232.6 retentions payable; contract assets 745.5 against billings in excess 990.2 and customer advances 726.8. Projected from DSO, retention and advance ratios off the revenue build, with no plug [SIGCM clause 4].

drivers.driver: Capital expenditure
drivers.justification: TOP-DOWN ON EVIDENCED ABSENCE. No forward capex plan, maintenance-capex disclosure or capital-commitments figure is published — only history (USD 52.3m FY2025, 75.1m FY2024, 50.9m H1-2026, plus associate contributions of 45.8m and 53.1m). Capex is therefore set as a percentage of revenue benchmarked to that history, split between maintenance and the named concession commitments, and sensitised.

drivers.driver: Distributions to shareholders
drivers.justification: TOP-DOWN ON EVIDENCED ABSENCE. The company paid twice a year without a break from 2020 to August 2025 (USD 0.47 per share, 51.8m, in FY2025) and then stopped: the 13 May 2026 AGM notice and board resolution carry NO distribution resolution, the IR history table's last entry is August 2025, and H1-2026 paid nil against 24.2m in H1-2025. The pause is modelled explicitly through the OCI combination window rather than a payout ratio being extrapolated.

drivers.driver: Share count and the OCI combination
drivers.justification: Both cases come from the circular itself, not from an estimate: 110,243,935 shares standalone, and 207,445,294 after issuing 97,201,359 new shares at USD 1 nominal plus a USD 12.79 premium, with consideration shares at about 47% of the enlarged capital. The two cases are PUBLISHED SEPARATELY and dual-framed; the cash-settled LTIP adds no dilution to either.

drivers.driver: Currency mix of revenue and of debt
drivers.justification: Disclosed on both sides. Revenue: 88.7% of backlog is foreign currency or FCY-pegged against 11.3% EGP, with 75.2% of the Egypt backlog itself in FCY. Debt: the note-18 borrower list gives the tranche domiciles and note 6.3 gives the EUR and EGP monetary positions and their sensitivities. FX-denominated debt is carried at its local-equivalent cost rather than a raw coupon [SIGCM clause 3], and the net EGP monetary SHORT is modelled as a gain on devaluation alongside the equity translation loss.

drivers.driver: Backlog burn rate and book-to-bill
drivers.justification: Calibrated from the disclosed backlog and award series against audited revenue: backlog 5.5 / 8.1 / 7.6 / 9.0 / 10.9 USD bn at FY2022 through H1-2026 and new awards 3.6 / 5.8 / 3.0 / 5.6 / 4.8, against audited revenue of 4,177.3 / 3,367.5 / 3,254.9 / 5,049.8. Current cover is 2.15 years and H1-2026 book-to-bill is 1.62x. The burn rate is solved per region, not group-wide, because MEA and USA convert at visibly different speeds.

drivers.driver: Discount rate (WACC) — build and cross-check
drivers.justification: The build is USD-based to match the reporting currency and the 88.7% FCY backlog. Two disclosed corridors bracket it and are used as CROSS-CHECKS, never as inputs: management's own goodwill-test WACCs of 9.0% USA and 22.2% MENA with terminal growth of 2.1% and 5.1%, and the independent valuer BDO's OC-wide range of 14.6%-17.6% with 3.0% terminal growth used to strike the OCI exchange ratio. A study WACC outside that corridor has to be argued in the text.

drivers.driver: Equity beta — regressor selection (NOT resolved in this sweep)
drivers.justification: The company's own filings and IR page establish which regressors are even eligible: ADX in AED (primary, ISIN AEE01702O253) and EGX in EGP (secondary, ISIN EGS95001C011). The series held in this repo, engine/raw_ohlc/EG/ORAS.csv, closes at 782.25 — the EGP magnitude, against the company's own simultaneous quotes of EGP 855.85 and AED 60.30 — so it is the EGX series and its conforming regressor is engine/raw_indices/EG/EGX30.csv. THE BETA ITSELF IS NOT COMPUTED HERE and must come from engine/beta_regression.own_stock_beta(); the build must also handle the Nasdaq-Dubai-to-ADX migration inside the window and the EGP's own move over it.
